offence_severity: 3 years to 6 years for Section 409 and 477A of IPC; 2 years plus penalty of Rs.10,000/- for Section 5(1)(c) and (d) of P.C. Act
number_of_offences: Charged with multiple offences under Sections 409, 477A, and 5(1)(c) and (d) of P.C. Act; convictions upheld for all
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as the accused conspired to misappropriate fertilizers and falsify records
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the prosecution's case that the accused conspired to misappropriate 1040 bags of urea, falsified records, and made false entries in the gate register and other forms to show delivery of the fertilizer when it was not actually delivered.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the witnesses' credibility by considering the totality of oral and documentary evidence, noting inconsistencies in some testimonies but ultimately relying on the evidence to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 24.03.1980; Trial judgment: 26.09.1997; High Court decision: 17.02.2009; Supreme Court decision: 28.02.2019
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Santosh Mishra, Manish Kumar, Ms. Sharmila Upadhyay, Ms. Aparajita Singh, T. Mahipal; Counsel for the State: P.K. Dey, A.K. Srivastava, Arvind Kumar Sharma, Ashok Kumar Srivastava
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction affirmed; High Court: Conviction confirmed with reduced sentence; Supreme Court: Appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants conspired and misappropriated 1040 bags of urea, falsifying records to show delivery at FCI godown at Tilrath, despite no actual delivery.
defence_argument: The defence contended that the prosecution failed to prove misappropriation of 1040 bags, relying on inconsistent evidence and that the FIR was based on only 540 bags, not 1040.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, considering the totality of oral and documentary evidence.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, and the courts found the findings of the trial and appellate courts to be correct.
